title: The ECB Hold and the Two-Sided Margin Squeeze
trigger: On 29 October the ECB kept deposit, main refinancing and marginal lending rates at 2.50%, 2.65% and 2.90%. It warned that higher energy prices could lift inflation and weaken growth.
limitations: All balance-sheet amounts, betas and shocks are hypothetical. Parallel instantaneous repricing assumes a one-year static balance sheet, no hedges, floors, behavioural deposits, credit migration or FX. September HICP is an earlier release and is not an October flash estimate.
formula: Illustrative annual ΔNII (€m) = rate shock (bp)/10,000 × [rate-sensitive assets × asset beta − rate-sensitive liabilities × liability beta]. The model is a first-order sensitivity, not a forecast or a bank-specific asset-liability model.
decision: Monitor deposit and asset repricing betas alongside stress-driven liquidity migration. Avoid extrapolating the ECB’s unchanged decision into a forecast of future rates.
worked_example: Illustrative worked example: €1.5bn of assets, €1.3bn of liabilities, a +100bp parallel shock, 50% asset beta and 65% deposit beta yield −€0.95m annual ΔNII. The deposit beta break-even is approximately 57.7%.
